chapter.name: Power Play
chapter.blurb: Exponential notation, the laws of exponents for multiplication and division, zero and negative exponents, powers of 10 and scientific notation.

scope_in.item: Exponential notation n to the power a as n multiplied by itself a times, with base and exponent named
Reading powers aloud, e.g. n cubed or n raised to the power 4, and writing products of letter-numbers such as a cubed b squared
Exponential growth through repeated doubling, e.g. paper folding where 10 folds multiply thickness 1024 times
Counting combinations with powers, e.g. a 5-digit lock giving 10 to the power 5 passwords
Multiplying powers with the same base: n to the a times n to the b equals n to the a plus b
A power raised to a power: n to the a, all raised to b, equals n to the a times b
Powers with the same exponent: n to the a times m to the a equals n times m, all to the a
Dividing powers with the same base: n to the a divided by n to the b equals n to the a minus b, with n not zero
The zero exponent, n to the power 0 equals 1 for any non-zero n, derived from the division rule
Negative exponents: n to the minus a equals 1 over n to the a, and n to the a equals 1 over n to the minus a
Writing whole numbers and decimals in expanded form using powers of 10, including 10 to the power 0
Scientific notation x times 10 to the y, where x is at least 1 and less than 10 and y is any integer

scope_out.item: Fractional and rational exponents such as a half power
scope_out.reason: Only integer exponents appear in this chapter

scope_out.item: Logarithms as the inverse of exponentiation
scope_out.reason: A later topic; this chapter never inverts a power

scope_out.item: Surds and irrational numbers arising from roots
scope_out.reason: Belongs with square and cube roots in Chapter 1 and with Class 9 number systems
Growth is explored numerically here, never as a graphed function

scope_out.item: Significant figures and rounding rules for scientific notation
scope_out.reason: The chapter writes numbers in standard form but sets no precision rules

concepts.name: Exponential notation, base and exponent
concepts.description: Writing repeated multiplication as a power, naming the base and the exponent, and reading powers correctly.
concepts.idea: Repeated multiplication gets long very quickly, so we write how many times the number is multiplied as a small raised number.
concepts.rule: n to the power a means n multiplied by itself a times. In 5 to the power 4, the base is 5 and the exponent is 4, and its value is 625.
concepts.example: Folding a sheet 10 times doubles its thickness each time, so the thickness increases 2 to the power 10 = 1024 times.

concepts.name: Multiplying powers and raising a power to a power
concepts.description: The rules n to the a times n to the b equals n to the a plus b, and a power of a power multiplying the exponents.
concepts.idea: Multiplying powers of the same base just stacks the repeated factors together, so the counts of factors add.
concepts.rule: n to the a times n to the b equals n to the a plus b. A power raised to a power multiplies the exponents. Powers with the same exponent combine as n to the a times m to the a equals n times m, all to the a.
concepts.example: 3 to the 4 times 3 to the 3 is 81 times 27 = 2187, which is 3 to the power 7.

concepts.name: Dividing powers and the zero exponent

concepts.name: Powers of 10 and expanded form

concepts.idea: Our place-value system is built on powers of 10, so every digit's place is a power of 10.

concepts.example: 47561 equals 4 times 10 to the 4, plus 7 times 10 cubed, plus 5 times 10 squared, plus 6 times 10 to the 1, plus 1 times 10 to the 0.
